How to read this analysis

  • Each paper contributes at most once per keyword. A paper may mention many keywords; shares do not sum to 100%.
  • Unigrams and adjacent two/three-word phrases are extracted after removing English stopwords, mathematical markup, and generic prose. An editable dictionary merges selected synonyms and plurals.
  • Monthly share = matching papers / all papers in that cohort and month. Zero-paper months have an undefined share, not zero.
  • Emergence compares the recent window with all earlier complete months. The score is excess recent papers above the baseline rate multiplied by log₂ of the smoothed share ratio. Smoothing is (matches + 0.5)/(papers + 1). It is a descriptive ranking, not a significance test.
  • The canonical vocabulary combines an editable exact-match list with optional historically common terms learned separately for each cohort. Learned terms must reach the configured share threshold overall and in at least three baseline months (or all if fewer). Recent data never contributes to this learned set. Longer phrases containing canonical words remain eligible.
  • Discovery favors multiword terms supported in recent titles and multiple months. Nested phrases are collapsed only when they match identical paper sets. All settings and the explicit canonical list are recorded in manifest.json.
  • The minimum document count is 5. Emergence cloud sizes reflect score; frequency-context clouds reflect paper counts. Sizes are relative within each panel; compare exact percentages in tables.
  • The general share-change tables compare the last 3 complete calendar months with the preceding 3, weighted by paper counts. Sparse terms can fluctuate sharply.
  • Dates are original submissions (version 1), while titles and abstracts are the latest metadata returned by arXiv. Revisions may change historical keyword counts.
  • Coverage is checked against API totals, with one record per arXiv ID. Complete retrieval means all indexed matches at retrieval time; indexing delays can still affect recent dates.
  • This measures language and topic attention, not scientific quality, citations, or proven research impact. The Lindblad screen can miss implicit descriptions and include incidental mentions.
